narrative.overview:
The next event is a boarding pass: one sheet of paper on a slate ground, with the leave time below a tear line that counts down to the door. Everything else waits on a departure board beside it, ruled rows that rank themselves by time. The system is built to be read in two seconds from across a room, so the pass is the only object, the board is only lines, and colour appears when it changes what the owner does next.

Density is low and sizes are large. One paper object, one column of rows and one strip of live trains fill the frame, and a row that does not fit waits for the next page. The world refuses the grid of equal widget panels. Certainty is visible: a live time is heavy and punched, an estimate is lighter, dashed and labelled "about".

Provisional: this system was recorded from a build on real data, with the AI box still to connect. The data shape behind it (including `leaveIn`, `estimate`, `change`, `train.line`, `night` and the row kinds) is a stand-in and may be renamed. The visual rules hold; the field names do not.
keyCharacteristics: One paper pass on slate, holding the next event and the leave time.
A tear of 30 notches, one per minute, that doubles as the countdown.
Board rows on hairlines in a fixed column grid, with no panels.
One red family, spent on changes that hold until tapped.
A weight, a dash and the word "about" mark every estimate.
The whole frame scales in rem from one 1280x800 reference.

rules.name: The One Alarm Rule
rules.body: The red family marks changes, and nothing else competes with it. The one extension is the loss of live trains, a text-only line, because that changes every time on the board. A failed AI request is not a change and stays neutral.

rules.name: The Line Takes the Stub Rule
rules.body: Within five minutes of leaving, on an exact time, the stub fills with the train line's colour. Outside that window the stub is plain paper. An estimate never takes the colour.

rules.name: The Higher Ink Rule
rules.body: Stub text takes whichever of Pass Paper or Ink reads better on the line colour. That gives light text only on A/C/E, 7 and J/Z, and dark text on every other line. Line bullets are a separate matter: they keep the official livery, with white letters on all lines except the yellow N/Q/R/W.

rules.name: The Held Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number uses tabular figures, so clocks and countdowns never shift sideways. The CSS `font` shorthand resets this, so anything set with the shorthand that shows numbers must ask for tabular figures again.

rules.name: The Weight Is Certainty Rule
rules.body: A live time is 700. An estimated time is 500 in the same face and size. Weight alone never carries it: the dashed tear and "about" label go with it.

rules.name: The One Frame Rule
rules.body: All sizes are in rem and the root is `clamp(14px, min(1.25vw, 2vh), 24px)`, so the board scales as one frame from 16px at 1280x800. Nothing in the two-column layout is sized in pixels except hairline strokes.

rules.name: The Whole Row Rule
rules.body: The frame never scrolls and never cuts a row. Rows that do not fit are held back, a steel "N more" control shows the next page, the last page offers "Back to top", and the board returns to the first page by itself after 30 seconds.

rules.name: The One Lifted Thing Rule
rules.body: Only the pass has a shadow, and it loses it at night. If a second thing seems to need lift, it belongs on the board's lines instead.

rules.name: The Tear Is the Clock Rule
rules.body: The tear is a countdown, not decoration. Never use it as a divider on any other surface, and never show notches that are not counting real minutes.

rules.name: The Held Change Rule
rules.body: A change never times out. It stays lit until it is tapped, and a row keeps its change when it lifts onto the pass, so dismissing either clears both.

dos: Do make the next event the largest thing on screen, with the leave time at 7.375rem on the 16px root.
Do size everything in rem so the frame scales as one piece.
Do show an estimate with all three signs: weight 500, a dashed tear and an "about" label.
Do keep a change lit until it is tapped.
Do keep every wall control at 56px or more.
Do keep a row's identity when it moves, so reranks slide in place.
Do put the letter in every line bullet.
Do keep night as a darker, quieter version of the same layout.
donts: Don't add cards, panels or widget grids to the board. Its only fills are controls, the changed row and the toast.
Don't use the red family for AI failures, emphasis, deadlines or decoration. Alert red is not Line 1/2/3 red, and neither stands in for the other.
Don't use line colours outside bullets and the stub.
Don't give an estimate the line colour, the notch count or "Leave now".
Don't let the wall scroll or cut a row in half.
Don't add a second shadow, or blur or backdrop effects of any kind.
Don't round anything other than the pass, or make circles of anything other than bullets, notches and cut-outs.
Don't time a change out or clear it on a wake tap.
Don't treat the white-on-livery pairing of a bullet as a precedent for text colour elsewhere.
